about.title: Los Altos Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Los Altos may feel like a quiet corner of Santa Clara County, but its mix of tech offices, retail corridors along El Camino Real, and construction sites still generates its share of workplace injuries — falls, equipment accidents, vehicle-related incidents on routes like Foothill Expwy or near I-280. Most of the time, California workers' compensation is the only path against an employer, no matter who was at fault. But when a subcontractor, property owner, equipment manufacturer, or another driver contributed to the injury, a separate third-party claim may be possible alongside comp benefits. LawProactive doesn't practice law or handle claims directly — we simply connect injured Los Altos workers with an independent attorney who can look at the full picture, sort out what applies, and explain options without pressure or cost to start.

whyChoose.title: Why Los Altos Workers Reach Out to LawProactive

items.title: Third-Party Claims Beyond Workers' Comp
items.desc: When someone other than your employer — like a subcontractor, equipment maker, or another driver — contributed to your injury, a separate claim outside the workers' comp system may be available.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: California law makes it illegal for an employer to punish you for reporting a workplace injury, and understanding this protection matters before deciding how to move forward.

items.title: Clarity on Deadlines That Matter
items.desc: Employer injury reports are generally due within 30 days, while a third-party injury claim typically carries a 2-year filing deadline — an attorney can help you track both.

items.question: I was hurt on a construction site near Foothill Expwy — can I sue the property owner instead of just filing workers' comp?
items.answer: Possibly. If a property owner, contractor, or other party besides your employer contributed to the unsafe conditions, you may be able to pursue a third-party claim in addition to standard workers' compensation. An independent attorney can review the site details and determine who else might share responsibility.

items.question: How soon do I need to report a workplace injury in Los Altos?
items.answer: California generally requires injury reports to your employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate your workers' comp claim, so it's worth reporting promptly even if the injury seems minor at first.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for filing a workers' comp claim?
items.answer: No — retaliation for reporting a workplace injury or filing a claim is illegal under California law. If you believe you've faced retaliation, an attorney can help you understand your options alongside your injury claim.
